label: Clean a messy spreadsheet or CSV
whyItFits: DataMend Lab is purpose-built for inspecting dirty tables, standardizing inconsistent dates and text casing, flagging sentinel missing values (-999, 'N/A'), and exporting a clean CSV with a reproducible transformation log.
accomplishes: Detects mixed column types and strips embedded units (e.g., '4.35 mg/L' → 4.35)
Converts heterogeneous dates into canonical ISO-8601 format
Identifies exact and primary-key duplicates without silent deletion

label: Reshape wide tables or join multiple files
whyItFits: Statistical models and chart grammars require tidy data (one variable per column, one observational unit per row). DataMend Lab reshapes wide crosstabs into long tidy tables and audits relational joins.
accomplishes: Pivots wide month/category columns into tidy key-value rows
Audits unmatched keys and row multiplicity during table joins
Exports both the reshaped dataset and the equivalent R Tidyverse pipeline

label: Choose and build the right statistical chart
whyItFits: VisualGrammar classifies your variables (nominal, ordinal, discrete, continuous, time) and recommends chart structures ranked by the Cleveland–McGill perceptual hierarchy, ensuring a Lie Factor between 0.95 and 1.05.
accomplishes: Matches data shape and cardinality to the highest-accuracy visual channel
Compares histograms, boxplots, violin plots, and beeswarms side by side
Validates WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and deuteranopia/protanopia colorblind safety

label: Explore correlation, OLS regression & outliers
whyItFits: QuartetLab pairs an interactive bivariate scatterplot with a live Gram-Schmidt exact-moment solver, synchronized Residuals vs. Fitted and Normal Q-Q plots, and automatic Cook's distance (D_i > 4/n) outlier halos.
accomplishes: Manipulates data points at 60fps while observing or locking x̄, s_x, ȳ, s_y, r, and R²
Reveals how identical regression summaries can hide curvature or high-leverage points
Generates Minitab/R computer output tables and printable AP/undergraduate worksheets

label: Understand probability & sampling distributions
whyItFits: ResampleLab turns abstract probability and Central Limit Theorem formulas into visible Monte Carlo experiments, showing how sample statistics vary across repeated draws from known or empirical populations.
accomplishes: Visualizes the transition from a single sample (n) to a sampling distribution of B = 10,000 draws
Demonstrates how sample size (n) and population skewness affect standard error
Uses a deterministic PRNG seed so classroom demonstrations are 100% repeatable

label: Calculate a bootstrap confidence interval
whyItFits: ResampleLab resamples your observed dataset with replacement to build empirical bootstrap distributions for means, medians, trimmed means, proportions, or slopes—and compares Percentile, Studentized-t*, and Classical intervals side by side.
accomplishes: Constructs 90%, 95%, and 99% bootstrap confidence intervals with visual tail shading
Diagnoses when skewness invalidates symmetric normal-theory intervals
Exports bootstrap replicate distributions and R boot/infer scripts

label: Run a permutation or randomization hypothesis test
whyItFits: ResampleLab generates exact and Monte Carlo null reference distributions by shuffling group labels under exchangeability, making one-sided and two-sided empirical p-values transparent without relying on fragile parametric assumptions.
accomplishes: Visualizes null label shuffling for two-sample means, proportions, and matched pairs
Shades tail probabilities directly on the simulated null distribution
Separates statistical significance (p-value) from practical effect magnitude

label: Decompose a time series & forecast future values
whyItFits: ForecastLab decomposes chronological series into trend, seasonality, and remainder via STL, benchmarks ETS and SARIMA models against Seasonal Naïve using rolling-origin cross-validation (MASE), and plots calibrated 80%/95% prediction intervals.
accomplishes: Separates long-term trend (T_t) from recurring calendar seasonality (S_t)
Evaluates genuine out-of-sample forecast errors across rolling origins
Checks innovation residual autocorrelation (ACF) and exports forecast fan charts

label: Forecast a messy spreadsheet with date gaps
whyItFits: Forecasting models require a strictly ordered, regularly spaced time index. Start in DataMend Lab to standardize dates into ISO-8601 and audit missing periods, then export the clean CSV into ForecastLab for STL decomposition and ETS/SARIMA modeling.
accomplishes: Stage 1 (DataMend Lab): Coerces heterogeneous timestamps, removes duplicate dates, and flags explicit NA gaps
Stage 2 (ForecastLab): Fits ETS/SARIMA models on the regularized series and computes 80%/95% prediction intervals
Preserves full data provenance via exported CSV and transformation recipe
